subject: pathology
title: Ferroptosis, Autophagic Vacuolation, and Internucleosomal DNA Cleavage

steps.tx: An iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by the lethal accumulation of lipid peroxides within cell membranes represents ferroptosis. Uncontrolled **ferroptotic cell death** is initiated when intracellular free ferrous iron participates in Fenton chemistry, producing hydroxyl radicals that attack polyunsaturated fatty acid residues in membrane phospholipids.
steps.say: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by toxic membrane lipid peroxidation.

vis.caption: Severe microvesicular steatosis illustrating defective mitochondrial lipid metabolism and peroxidation.
vis.alt: Hepatic microvesicular fatty infiltration and metabolic oxidative stress

steps.tx: Under physiological conditions, ferroptosis is actively repressed by glutathione peroxidase four, a selenoprotein that converts toxic lipid hydroperoxides into non-toxic lipid alcohols. Inhibition of cystine-glutamate antiporter system Xc- deprives the cell of cysteine, depleting intracellular glutathione and inactivating **glutathione peroxidase 4**, triggering lethal ferroptosis.
steps.say: Depleting cysteine halts glutathione production, inactivating GPX4 and precipitating ferroptosis.

nodes.label: Inhibition of System Xc- (e.g., Erastin) Halts Intracellular Cystine Uptake
Cysteine Starvation Depletes Cellular Reduced Glutathione (GSH) Pools
Glutathione Peroxidase 4 (GPX4) Loses Cofactor and Ceases Activity
Toxic Lipid Reactive Oxygen Species Accumulate, Destroying Membrane Lipids

steps.tx: Ultrastructural examination of ferroptotic cells reveals pathognomonic morphological alterations confined specifically to mitochondria. While the cell nucleus remains structurally normal without pyknosis or chromatin marginalization, the mitochondria display **shrunken condensed volume**, increased inner membrane density, and vanishing of mitochondrial cristae.
steps.say: Ferroptosis characteristically produces shrunken mitochondria with dense membranes and loss of cristae.

left.title: Ferroptosis Morphology
points: Mitochondria appear abnormally shrunken with condensed matrix
Loss and dissolution of internal mitochondrial cristae
Outer mitochondrial membrane ruptures under lipid stress
Nucleus remains structurally intact without chromatin marginalization

right.title: Apoptosis Morphology
points: Cellular shrinkage with prominent peripheral membrane blebbing
Condensation and peripheral crescentic margination of chromatin
Fragmentation into membrane-enclosed apoptotic bodies
Mitochondria exhibit outer membrane permeabilization without shrinkage

steps.tx: During conditions of nutrient starvation, growth factor withdrawal, or metabolic stress, cells initiate an evolutionary conserved lysosomal degradation pathway known as autophagy. Operating as an essential survival mechanism, **autophagic self-digestion** sequesters senescent organelles and misfolded protein aggregates into double-membrane vesicles for recycling into metabolic intermediates.
steps.say: Autophagy sequesters damaged organelles into double-membrane vesicles to recycle metabolic nutrients.

vis.caption: Ischemic parenchymal injury demonstrating intense cellular metabolic stress before irreversible infarction.
vis.alt: Splenic infarction showing severe cellular metabolic starvation and necrosis

steps.tx: The molecular nucleation of autophagy begins with an isolated crescent-shaped membrane cistern termed the phagophore. Mediated by the Beclin-1 complex, the phagophore expands and engulfs cytoplasmic targets, sealing to form a mature **double-membrane autophagosome** that decorates its outer surface with microtubule-associated protein light chain three.
steps.say: The phagophore expands around cytoplasmic targets to seal into a double-membrane autophagosome.

nodes.label: Nutrient Starvation Inhibits mTOR Complex 1, Activating ULK1 Complex
Beclin-1/VPS34 Generates PI3P to Nucleate Crescent-Shaped Phagophore

Membrane Encloses Cargo to Form Closed Double-Membrane Autophagosome

steps.tx: Following closure, the autophagosome moves along microtubule tracks to fuse with a primary lysosome, forming an autophagolysosome. Inside this acidic compartment, **lysosomal acid hydrolases** degrade the sequestered contents, releasing free amino acids, fatty acids, and nucleosides back into the cytosol to fuel essential cellular energy requirements.
steps.say: Autophagosomes fuse with lysosomes, allowing acid hydrolases to digest contents into reusable nutrients.

left.title: Macroautophagy
points: Major form involving de novo sequestration by double-membrane autophagosomes
Engulfs entire organelles like damaged mitochondria (mitophagy)
Fuses with lysosomes to form acidic single-membrane autolysosomes
Governed by conserved autophagy-related (ATG) gene products

right.title: Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy
points: Direct translocation of individual soluble cytosolic proteins into lysosomes
Requires recognition of specific KFERQ-like pentapeptide motifs
Hsp70 chaperone binds cargo and docks at lysosomal LAMP-2A receptors
Translocates unfolded target directly across lysosomal membrane

steps.tx: A definitive molecular distinction separating apoptotic cell death from random necrotic autolysis is the pattern of genomic DNA cleavage. On agarose gel electrophoresis, apoptotic DNA resolves into a sharp **internucleosomal DNA ladder** consisting of integer multiples of one hundred and eighty to two hundred base-pair fragments.
steps.say: Agarose gel electrophoresis shows an internucleosomal ladder in apoptosis, unlike the necrotic smear.

left.title: Apoptotic DNA Laddering
points: Driven by caspase-activated DNase (CAD) cleaving at exposed linkers
Nucleosomal histone cores protect wrapped 146 base pairs of DNA
Generates discrete ladder bands of 180, 360, 540, and 720 base pairs
Pathognomonic molecular electrophoretic hallmark of programmed apoptosis

right.title: Necrotic DNA Smear
points: Driven by uncontrolled release of non-specific lysosomal nucleases
Random, non-specific enzymatic cleavage across all genomic regions
Generates continuous distribution of random-sized DNA fragments
Appears on agarose gel electrophoresis as a diffuse continuous smear

steps.tx: The internucleosomal ladder pattern arises because chromosomal DNA is wrapped around histone octamers in repeating nucleosomal units. While the one hundred and forty-six base pairs wrapped around each nucleosome are protected from enzymatic attack, the **unprotected linker DNA** between nucleosomes is accessible to caspase-activated DNase cleavage.
steps.say: Caspase-activated DNase selectively cleaves unprotected linker DNA between nucleosomes, generating the ladder.
